The actual distance measured by the steel tape is corrected for thermal expansion using the coefficient of linear expansion for steel (1.2×10⁻⁵ /°C). The measured reading is 35.794 m at 35°C, while the tape was calibrated at 20°C, giving a temperature difference of 15°C. The actual distance is 35.794 × (1 + 1.2×10⁻⁵ × 15) = 35.800 m (rounded to five significant figures).

For the solar collector at Regina (latitude 50°N) at noon on the summer solstice, the solar declination is 23.5°N, so the zenith angle is 50° − 23.5° = 26.5°. The fraction of the standard solar flux (direct normal irradiance) available to a horizontal collector is the cosine of the zenith angle, cos(26.5°) ≈ 0.8949.

ANSWER: 35.800,0.8949
